---
title: "Research"
---

My research is in theoretical condensed matter physics, with an emphasis on quantum geometry, topology, symmetry, and nonlinear response phenomena. I mainly use tight-binding models and symmetry-based analysis to identify robust transport and optical effects.

## Quantum geometry and nonlinear responses

I study how geometric properties of Bloch states appear in measurable nonlinear responses. This includes the divergence of shift-current responses near a two-dimensional Weyl-semimetal limit [@yoshida2025diverging], the emergent-gravity Hall effect associated with quantum geometry [@yoshida2025emergent], and light-induced magnetization generated by quantum-geometric effects [@yoshida2026light].

## Altermagnets and spin photovoltaic effects

A major recent direction is nonlinear spin transport in altermagnetic systems. In particular, I developed a theoretical framework for a quantized spin-current analogue of the circular photogalvanic effect in altermagnetic Weyl semimetals, combining symmetry classification with tight-binding modeling [@yoshida2026quantization].

## Two-dimensional Weyl semimetal limits

I have studied discontinuous changes of electric polarization around topological phase transitions in two-dimensional systems, including symmetry breaking in two-dimensional Weyl semimetals [@yoshida2023breaking] and polarization jumps across topological phase transitions [@yoshida2023topological].

## Magnetoelastic waves

I also work on coupled magnetic and elastic excitations in ferromagnetic thin films, including magnetoelastic waves mediated by dipolar interactions [@yoshida2026magnetoelastic].
